#3395. Gentler Streak 6.0 adds a new wellbeing timeline and customizable dashboard

In an update rolling out today, Gentler Streak is introducing new ways for users to track their wellbeing and personalize the app’s guidance based on how they feel. Here are the details.

One of my favorite exercise-tracking apps got even better today with an update that expands its functionality beyond workouts and fitness metrics to better reflect how users actually feel.

Starting today, Gentler Streak will let users log how they feel each day, including their mood, symptoms, and other factors that may not be reflected in their health and fitness data.

Some days, the way we feel isn’t reflected in what the data says, no matter the data quality. “How I Feel” captures the part that devices can’t grasp: personal context. And how you feel is not only a mood: it is also a sore throat, heavy legs or a poor night’s sleep. The feature was inspired by the Gentler Streak community, including people living with chronic fatigue, fibromyalgia, ADHD, and those not wearing their Apple Watch at night. Without overnight signals, their guidance has less to work with.

According to the team behind Gentler Streak, these new features are aimed at users whose health and fitness data may not accurately reflect how they feel, including those dealing with chronic conditions, menopause, stress, or poor sleep.

In practice, the app will now feature four tabs: Today, Health, Workouts, and Insights. In the Today and Health tabs, a new “Anything to add?” field will let users rate how they feel, from Great to Off, and add context about what might be affecting their well-being, including fatigue, feeling calm, or custom tags.

You decide when the prompt appears. Go to Profile > Settings > Self-Evaluation Prompt and choose one of three options: only when your vitals or sleep are off, always on, or never.

Gentler Stories notes that the self-assessments will override the app’s wellbeing estimates for that day, with its daily guidance adjusting accordingly.

The Today tab will also feature an expanded 10- or 30-day timeline showing logged workouts, wellbeing estimates, potential symptoms, poor sleep or vitals, and the first day of a menstrual period, while Health will introduce an interactive chart showing users how their wellbeing changes over time, with the ability to filter by symptoms.

Users can now also customize which information appears on their Today screen, including vitals, sleep, steps, menstrual cycle, VO₂ max, and workouts, which is a nice touch.

For users who are sick, injured, or taking a break from exercise, the app’s hallmark Activity Path will make way for a new Wellbeing Path, which lets them track their wellbeing on a daily basis.

For users with Active status, a new colorful wellbeing line will appear beneath the Activity Path, reflecting how they feel each day. This information is logged automatically for those who wear their Apple Watch overnight, or based on self-assessments for those who don’t.

Importantly, Gentler Stories notes that all information entered through the new feature remains on the user’s device, with no accounts or company-operated servers involved.

Gentler Streak is available for free on the App Store, with in-app purchases for monthly, yearly, family, and lifetime subscriptions.

#3394. Inside the Wild Nights of Martin Scorsese and Robbie Robertson’s 1970s L.A. Adventure

In 1976, Martin Scorsese was riding high — figuratively and literally. The filmmaker had just scored a massive hit with Taxi Driver, and was about to embark on his most ambitious project yet: the moody, downbeat musical New York, New York. A story of a mercurial artist and his wife (played by Robert DeNiro and Liza Minnelli), this follow-up to his award-winning movie was one part homage to the MGM musicals of Scorsese’s youth and one part deconstruction of the genre’s forget-your-troubles-come-on-get-happy ethos. Before the production was finished, art would end up imitating life and this tale of temoper tantrums and troubled marriages would start playing out in real life. The fact that Scorsese had begun “dabbling” with cocaine around this point did not help smooth things out at all.

It was shortly after Scorsese had started filming New York, New York that he got an offer he could not refuse: Did he want to head out to San Francisco and film the farewell performance of the Band on Thanksgiving? The result would be one of the greatest concert movies of all time. And it would also result in Scorsese befriending the group’s singer, songwriter and lead guitarist Robbie Robertson. Their lifelong bond would be cemented shortly after, when the two men found themselves unexpectedly single and decided to move in together. The ensuing debauchery has since become the stuff of 1970s movie-nerd lore. It also put Scorsese in the hospital and nearly killed him.

In this excerpt from Just a Shot Away, writer and Rolling Stone contributor Mark Binelli’s warts-and-all look at Scorsese’s career (on shelves now), we rewind back to the moment when Marty met Robbie — and an era of late nights, marathon movie-watching, excessive partying and dangerous behavior began in earnest.**

Jonathan Taplin reached out during the summer of 1976, 10 days into the shooting of New York, New York. He’d reconnected with the Band. The guys were planning an all-star farewell concert on Thanksgiving at the Winterland Ballroom, the promoter Bill Graham’s San Francisco venue. Marty had obviously moved well beyond the concert-documentary phase of his career, but might he consider filming the proceedings?

Not long after, Taplin recalled, he and Robbie Robertson visited Marty at his office on the MGM lot. “He was living a very crazy existence,” Taplin said. “First off, he was having an affair with Liza Minnelli. And yet his wife, Julia Cameron, was around on the set all the time. So he was constantly ducking out. He had a dressing room on the MGM lot that had a daybed in it. It was very, very weird. It was insane. And they were all doing so much coke.” Steve Prince (“a kind of hangout guy, driver, bodyguard, and coke dealer”) had firmly become “part of the entourage” by that point, Taplin added. “He was the guy who would stand outside of Marty’s trailer on the set of New York, New York and bar the door.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

Later, Robbie met with Marty over dinner at the Mandarin, an upscale Chinese restaurant in Beverly Hills, at the time a novelty. In an auspice of their future partnership-in-crime, each man brought along his wife and girlfriend, in Marty’s case, Julia and Liza, in Robbie’s, his wife, Dominique Bourgeois, a Québécois journalist, and her friend Geneviève Bujold, the actress. Marty, the music fanatic, held Robbie somewhat in awe: They were the same age, but Robbie had joined the Band at 16 and had been woodshedding with Dylan when Marty was still an anonymous film student struggling to complete his second short. Robbie took note of Marty’s intense gaze that night, given a slightly devilish cast by his dark Vandyke beard. Later he would say, of possible directors, that Marty “was the only person that knew enough about the fucking music and grew up on it just like me, and was basically just as much a punk as the rest of us. He could relate to the whole fucking thing.”

After dinner, they hit On the Rox, an after-hours bar on Sunset Boulevard, upstairs from the Roxy nightclub, which had become a clubhouse and discreet drug spot for hard-partying celebrities like John Lennon, Jack Nicholson, and Harry Nilsson. They started talking about documenting the concert “on a small level, maybe just video or 16mm,” Robbie said. Marty knew United Artists and the producers of New York, New York would never allow him to moonlight on another film, even a documentary, simultaneously. Then again, hadn’t John Huston managed to sneak off for big-game safaris during the filming of The African Queen? Couldn’t Marty slip away with a film crew over Thanksgiving weekend, when the New York, New York production would be on holiday anyway, not to shoot an elephant but a simple rock concert? As Robbie revealed the guests he’d invited to perform — Dylan, Muddy Waters, Van Morrison, Joni Mitchell, Neil Young — Marty stopped pretending to fight. What the hell would the studio do, fire him? Related Content Charli XCX to Cameo in Martin Scorsese’s New Horror Film With Leonardo DiCaprio, Jennifer Lawrence Amy Helm Allegedly Caused $2 Million in Damages to Levon Helm Studios, Lawsuit Claims 50 Years Ago Today: The Band Warm Up for ‘The Last Waltz’ in Asbury Park Levon Helm’s Family Embroiled in Dispute Over His Famed Woodstock Venue

Seeds of the pair’s drug buddydom were also sown that night. Robbie and Marty had been “sneaking in and out of the bathroom as if we all had weak bladders,” Robbie said. “Trying to be very proper.” At a certain point, Marty, who seemed to have a nasty cold, asked if anyone had nasal spray. Robbie gave him a look, unsure if he was cool or not, then decided to risk it. “This might help clear it up,” he said, producing a vial of coke a friend had just palmed him. Marty shook his head. “I’ve got that. I just need some Afrin or something.” He’d actually meant nasal spray. Neither man would be so basic as to quote the ending of Casablanca, but come on. The beginnings of beautiful friendships aren’t so common they should pass unnoted.

Production paused for Thanksgiving break, and as planned, Marty went up to San Francisco to film the Band’s Last Waltz concert. A director in a more reasonable frame of mind (unclouded by cocaine megalomania) might have thought, Okay, I’m already contractually bound to complete the biggest feature film of my career, and I’m technically sneaking off to work on this other dubious project, so I should probably keep things relatively low-key. Robbie had initially suggested simply shooting in 16mm, after all. Instead, Marty storyboarded the entire production in advance based on the set list (timing shots down to specific lyrics and instrumental passages), convinced set designer Boris Leven to dress up the Winterland Ballroom with props from the San Francisco Opera, and brought along seven cinematographers (including László Kovács, Michael Chapman, and Vilmos Zsigmond, who would go on to DP Michael Cimino’s The Deer Hunter) to film the entire thing in 35mm, which had been Kovács’ idea. “Can the cameras even shoot that long?” Marty had asked. “You won’t know unless you try,” Kovács said.

During much of the postproduction of New York, New York, Marty had also begun crafting a cut of The Last Waltz. Everyone involved agreed the 35mm footage of the show looked amazing, in this case Marty’s big swing had paid off, they had something, and he glimpsed a shot at redemption for having been fired from Woodstock all those years ago — he would make the greatest concert film of all time! They had too much, in fact, the concert having lasted over six hours — multiply that by seven cameras — but also, somehow, not enough: Robbie Robertson realized the concert had failed to represent a pair of key influences on the Band, country music and gospel. (The original concert had been “too lily-white,” the Band’s Levon Helm later said.) So the same week in May that Star Wars came out, Marty and the musicians reassembled on an MGM soundstage to record additional material with the Staple Singers and Emmylou Harris. Marty also filmed interviews with the members of the Band at Shangri-La, their studio in Malibu.

During a production meeting at the house on Mulholland Drive, Robbie and Marty discovered their personal lives happened to be falling apart in tandem. “You know, my wife threw me out, she left me, I have nowhere to go,” Robbie blurted out, admitting that he’d been crashing at hotels and occasionally at Shangri-La. In his posthumous memoir, he described the spontaneous confession as “embarrassing,” given that Marty “came from a certain place and culture where you didn’t reveal personal things.” But Marty surprised him. “‘You could stay here if you want!’ He leaned in, speaking more quietly. ‘Julia just moved out. She’s gone. It’s just Steve and me.’”

A Hollywood bachelor pad! There was plenty of room, and such proximity would be useful for any questions that might arise during The Last Waltz edit and sound mix. A splendid arrangement. How could it possibly go sideways? “It didn’t take but a day or two to fall into this process,” Robbie said, with his Canadian accent pronouncing the “pro” like someone talking sports. “We were like animals sniffing around for the trail, and hit it real quick, and it went into this thing kind of automatically. Those other voids that had been there in our lives were totally consumed. You couldn’t think of anything else but what was going on. It was very urgent, boom boom boom, one after the other, in, out, people in, people out, this movie, this studio, music, film, just full steam ahead.”

Full steam ahead. He’s being intentional in his vagueness because so much of their friendship revolved around things friends knew better than to discuss outside the inner circle, because in real life Marty and Robbie had become more than friends, they’d become drug buddies, which is a different kind of friendship, it’s a conspiracy — you and your mate versus the straight world, constantly on the make, constantly trying to figure out where to cop and who has what and where you might be able to duck into a toilet stall or back room or secluded corner table, and it all becomes incredibly serious and important-seeming, but also? It’s pretty funny. So many squares wandering around with no fucking clue what you and your drug buddy are getting up to. You’re pulling one over on the world! And every so often, if someone does seem to have your number, there’s a pleasing bit of frisson, an unspoken moment of comity. Oh, you get it too?

The great drug-buddy duo of literature, drawn from real life and embellished in a way that felt hilarious and true to anyone who has ever been one, remains Raoul Duke and Dr. Gonzo — Hunter S. Thompson and Oscar Zeta Acosta — in Thompson’s Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas. Describing a work of art as being like “____ on acid” has been a tired formulation for at least three decades, but in this case it’s literal and straightforward: Duke and Gonzo were Laurel and Hardy, Abbott and Costello — choose your favorite slapstick pairing — on acid. Thompson fashioned his adventures in the mode of a classic comedy team, and Robbie and Marty, who had seen those pictures and almost certainly read Thompson, Marty having at one point considered directing a Fear and Loathing script by Larry McMurtry, carried on the tradition, only in their case they were Hope and Crosby on coke and Quaaludes.

Robbie soon began calling Marty “Maestro,” lovingly fucking with him, with his self-conception of his work as within the tradition of the Great Directors. But he also meant it.

In his memoir, Robbie dated the fateful production meeting to February 1977, about five months before Julia described retrieving her typewriter from the house she “shared with Martin” in her own book. Given the degree of drug and alcohol consumption in their respective scenes, neither narrator can necessarily claim the mantle of greater reliability. The public record, with its numerous examples of the Scorseses appearing together as a couple throughout the period in question, would seem to support Julia’s timeline. But given the history of Hollywood publicity machines manufacturing happy facades, it’s certainly not dispositive, what with so much riding on the success of New York, New York and the likelihood of studio preference for minimal drama surrounding the director of an already troubled production.

Another record of this period, previously undiscovered, comes via [longtime Scorsese collaborator] Mardik Martin, who spent a fair amount of time at the Mulholland house and, with the initial cooperation of Marty, Robbie, and other witnesses and active participants, later began work on a script about that mysterious nocturnal period of their lives, one in which Marty, most of all, descended into what can only be described as a kind of madness — engaging in multiple overlapping love affairs, consuming heroic amounts of cocaine, rarely sleeping, harboring (literal) messianic delusions, and in the end very nearly dying. Mardik’s unfilmed script (dated April 15, 1985) and notes capture those lost years in granular and intimate fullness. His writing practice incorporated extensive research, which for this script meant recording and transcribing hours of interviews with the cast of characters, including Marty, Robbie, Steve Prince, and Isabella Rossellini, who became Marty’s lover and eventual third wife. Famous people employ publicists to quash these sorts of stories, and Mardik’s fealty to reality in his scénario à clef ultimately contributed to the project’s demise. And so he filed his tapes and pages away, where they remained unseen until several years after his death in 2019. The material called back to seedy Hollywood tales of the past, this time with mountains of blow and a rock and roll soundtrack.

The unmade film had the perfect title: Mardik called his script Insomnia.

In the script for Insomnia, Mardik described the Mulholland house as “a large, unpretentiously luxurious dwelling, sparsely but tastefully furnished. Rare and beautiful movie posters dominate wall spaces.” Robbie had been touched by the spontaneity and kindness in Marty’s offer of a bed and soon enough settled into the screening room, a converted garage with a screen, projector, convertible sofa, and poster of Fritz Lang’s M. As roommates, he and Marty would eventually fall into a routine consumed by working and partying, the lines often blurry in a manner familiar to a touring musician like Robertson and more novel for an overscheduled motion-picture director, though Marty would prove a quick study. He was spending his days editing The Last Waltz at a production office at United Artists — they’d sold the film before its completion based on the quality of the concert footage — while Robbie bounced around various music studios handling production work on the soundtrack album and writing and recording a new suite for the film.

Marty being Marty, their parties on Mulholland involved not only drugs and women but marathon movie screenings. Home video had just come on the market, but Marty preferred to pick up film prints. At the studio, Robbie might receive a call from his new housemate excitedly detailing the double or triple feature he’d programmed for the evening, and, oh, by the way, what time did Robbie think he’d be home? An hour, an hour and a half, something like that? An hour later, on the dot, the phone would ring again. Where are you? The food is ready! They’d both just ditched their families, but Marty had become the wife in a Forties domestic comedy.

Not that Robbie felt henpecked. He adored what he took to calling their Odd Couple routine and looked forward to the nightly master classes.

Eventually, they hung a sheet of paper in the kitchen for the jotting of titles to screen, their version of a chore list. Sometimes Marty would insist upon slogging through a trashy B-picture to reach a single extraordinary scene. Robbie’s tastes ran more toward the classical art film, surrealists, and gloomy Swedes: Bergman, Buñuel, Jean Cocteau. Later, they would laugh, Marty told Mardik, about “how I’d invite girls to my house to watch movies and bore them to tears with endless conversation about films.”

To keep the dawn at bay for as long as possible, the vampires had Steve Prince, their Renfield, install special blackout blinds in the projection room and eventually throughout the entire house, a task Robbie said Steve approached as seriously as if he’d been placed in charge of the Manhattan Project. “From that point on,” Robertson wrote in his memoir, “most of our lives were lived in darkness.” If a movie was playing, no matter the time of day, the only light came from the screen. Geneviève Bujold told Women’s Wear Daily in December 1977 that she’d recently become acquainted with Marty through “a friend” and had been attending some of the late-night screenings, mentioning a double feature of The Uninvited (Lewis Allen, 1944), a ghost story, and Dodsworth (William Wyler, 1936), an adaptation of the Sinclair Lewis novel. The old projector made “so much noise even the neighbors can hear it squeaking,” Bujold said, and Marty would run “two or three films a night, one on top of another, whoosh.”

Whoosh! The drug scene at the Mulholland house “was more than you normally would see,” acknowledged Taplin, who wasn’t exactly naive, having worked with the Band when three of its five members had serious heroin addictions. “I mean, there were a lot of people taking a lot of cocaine at that time. That was the drug of choice at that point. It made people feel like they were the most genius people in the world. It was around. But Marty and Robbie’s situation was unusual.”

There may have been “a little tinge of an educational thing” for Marty as well, Robbie said, Robbie who’d been on the road since he was sixteen, at the tail end of the rockabilly era, when he started playing for Ronnie Hawkins, the Ontario-by-way-of-Arkansas wild man who told Robbie and the other future members of the Band he couldn’t offer much in the way of salary but promised they’d “get more pussy than Frank Sinatra.” Because they took drugs and grew out their hair and beards, the boys’ club of New Hollywood directors found themselves routinely portrayed as something akin to their musical heroes, but for the most part they were solitary, film-obsessed nerds. Disposable income and the license of quasi-bohemian artistry allowed them to inhabit a rock star–adjacent space. But it would take an actual rock star like Robbie to edify a relative novice like Marty when it came to the problems of fame, the privileges of celebrity, and how one might discreetly inhabit a life of excess without pushing away the spotlight. “He was always uptight,” Robbie said of his friend. “He couldn’t relax with the thing.” Robertson could speak in mobster code better than Marty himself.

By the time they moved in together, Robbie had recorded one of the great face-melting guitar solos of the 1950s (on Hawkins’s cover of Bo Diddley’s “Who Do You Love,” which Greil Marcus called “possibly the most menacing piece of rock ’n’ roll ever made”). He’d played guitar on Blonde on Blonde and been onstage with Dylan on the U.K. tour when the crowd yelled “Judas!” He’d drunk corn liquor with Sonny Boy Williamson and played in Jack Ruby’s Dallas nightclub in 1963 (alongside a one-armed go-go dancer) a month before the Kennedy assassination. And he had already written “Up on Cripple Creek,” “The Night They Drove Old Dixie Down,” “Chest Fever,” “The Shape I’m In,” “Caledonia Mission,” “The Weight” —

He just grinned and shook my hand. “No” was all he said

— songs that spoke to his generation while also sounding haunted and outside of time.

In the opening interview section of The Last Waltz, Marty sits stiffly in a sports coat and trim beard, asking questions he already knows the answers to and coaxing Robbie to speak in clippable sound bites. Robertson, meanwhile, in his brown leather jacket and unbuttoned canteloupe-colored shirt, comes across as relaxed and louche and doesn’t seem to take the exercise very seriously. Though in reality, of course, he’d been the driving force behind the concert and film. “Ask me that again,” he tells Marty at one point, leaning forward in his chair. As Marty repeats himself, Robbie’s eyes wander, and before the question is finished, he’s snatched a fly from the air, or pretended to.

Cool Robbie always marveled at the passionate intensity Marty seemed incapable of not bringing to every relationship. In general, Robbie, his latest date on his arm, was never sure what he might find back on Mulholland. Marty the mad Sicilian might be having a wild screaming match with one of his girlfriends. Robertson, per a transcript of one of his interviews with Mardik: “There will be glass flying and breaking and loud, crazy arguments. (Makes me think of so many, but let him tell you about them.)” In any case, Robbie dedicated himself to giving his friend, as he put it, “an education of the road,” a primer in “how to deal with all of that and let the good times roll.”

But he also understood that for Marty, the evening could not properly begin until he got home, so eventually feelings of guilt about working so late would creep into his consciousness and he would begin making excuses to people in the studio before heading back up to the Hollywood Hills. “The food is ready” almost always meant pizza from Two Guys from Sicily had arrived, their best delivery option, substandard for New York but passable for Los Angeles. (“Disgusting,” Robbie said.) The movies might not start until two or three in the morning, Marty being, as Robbie once said, a believer in “the same thing Napoleon believes, that anyone who sleeps more than three hours a night is a fool.” An important caveat to the movie start time being everything had to wrap before the sun came up, for dawn had become “a scary thing” to the Maestro, it meant something ominous. “Ask him what,” Robbie told Mardik.Dawn coming up, Marty said, “meant death.” Trending Stories Raye, Rosalía, and Ella Langley Lead 2027 Grammy Nominees Jennifer Lopez Teases New Music on ‘Fallon’: ‘This Does Feel Like a Happy Era’ Watch Buffalo Springfield Come Together for the First Time in Many Years Robert Pattinson Is the Next James Bond

To Robbie it just meant he better get some sleep.

#3393. 10 Hacks Every Reddit User Should Know

If you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit. From mainstream sports to niche crafts, it does seem that there's some kind of Reddit community for everyone. (And if there's not one, you can make one yourself.) If you're using Reddit, here are 10 hacks you should know about to improve your experience on the site.

Reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private. You can hide your posts, comments, and the subreddits you're a part of. If you want to do this, click your profile icon once you've logged in to Reddit, and go to Settings > Profile. Alternatively, you can follow the direct link to Reddit's profile settings page. Click the drop-down menu next to Content & Activity, and select Hide all. You should also turn off Online Status on the same page to stop people from seeing when you're using Reddit.

Old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI. Old Reddit looks dated, but it doesn't have infinite scrolling, distracting animations, and a bunch of features designed to increase the time you spend on the platform. It's no wonder that Reddit is making it harder to access this version of the site. As long as it's around, you should switch to Old Reddit for a cleaner reading experience. You can do that by going to Reddit Settings > Preferences and enabling Default to Old Reddit. You can also visit old.reddit.com, though you'll need to sign in for access

Many subreddits use custom themes that range from beautiful to borderline unusable. If you want a more consistent UI across the site, you should disable these custom subreddit styles. Go to Reddit Settings > Preferences and turn off Use community themes. If you're using Old Reddit, click the preferences button in the top-right corner, and under "display options," disable allow subreddits to show me custom themes.

A multireddit is a feed that shows posts from a customized group of subreddits. You can think of it as a way to break out of Reddit's algorithms, and create your own Reddit feed. I use multireddits to follow all sports-related subs I'm interested in. I even have one for gaming, and one for fountain pens. It's a great way to create interest-specific feeds, and if you make them private, no one else can see them. To create one, click the Create custom feed button in the left pane in new Reddit. In the Old Reddit design, click the Create button in the left pane. Be sure to select the Private button to keep it from showing up for others. You can add as many subreddits as you like to the list, and bookmark the feed to access it whenever you wish to.

Reddit has recently adopted an Instagram-like experience for its feeds. It removed the ability to sort posts by new, controversial, best, etc., and instead offers "For You" and "Following." If you dislike this change, you can bypass it. I use Reddit on mobile Safari, and I recommend an extension called Sink It for Reddit. It can automatically redirect you to Old Reddit, and there's a feature that optimizes it for mobile, which brings back the old sorting options. You can also use third-party apps such as RedReader for Android, or RDX for Reddit on an iPhone or iPad to restore the old sorting options for Reddit posts.

After all these years, Reddit's built-in search still leaves something to be desired—at least, on the surface. To find posts on Reddit faster, use search filters on the site. For instance, adding "title:" to your search will limit the results to post titles, and boolean operators such as AND, OR, and NOT also work for advanced searches on the site.

#3391. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang set to be fired, with Johny Srouji among possible replacements [U]

Following reports of a potential second affair – this time with a subordinate – Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang looks certain to be fired by the company’s board, probably later today (though he may be allowed to ‘resign’). Apple’s chief hardware officer Johny Srouji has been listed among the potential replacements, though this seems unlikely.

Update: As we predicted, he’s gone today and Kress was indeed named interim CEO …

For anyone who’s been away from the planet for the past fortnight, Huang’s affair with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy has been the main headline news in the tech press since it came to light at the end of last month. The New York Times broke the story on October 29, citing it then as “a close relationship.” Nvidia initially denied that the relationship was anything out of the ordinary.

That changed on November 8 when Huang publicly admitted to the affair. Nvidia’s shares dropped 5%, and the company’s board of directors opened an independent investigation. Further details emerged over the following days.

Things got even worse yesterday when the same paper reported that Huang had also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him.

It was already looking inevitable that he would be fired, and the latest revelation adds to the urgency. The Wall Street Journal reported that the board was meeting last night to discuss the CEO’s future. That future at Nvidia is likely to be measured in hours rather than days.

The board now needs to find a replacement, and Bloomberg provides a rundown on some of the potential candidates. CFO Colette Kress looks likely to head the list for at least an interim appointment. The paper names a number of other possibilities, including Apple’s chief hardware officer, Johny Srouji.

Srouji has led one of the most successful in-house silicon programs in the industry, overseeing the custom chips that power the iPhone, Mac and other Apple devices. His track record gives him deep credibility on chip design, product integration and long-term technology roadmaps. But much of his experience has been built inside Apple’s tightly controlled ecosystem, and he hasn’t been tested in the kind of high-profile salesmanship which Huang is famous for.

Given the urgency, my money is on Nvidia announcing Kress as at least interim CEO, if not a permanent replacement. It seems exceedingly unlikely that Srouji would be appointed at this time, given the in-depth negotiations and discussions that would need to take place.

As to whether he’s a potential candidate following an interim appointment, it still seems unlikely. There was an earlier report of his claimed dissatisfaction at the company, but it seems a stretch to imagine him jumping ship so soon after his promotion to chief hardware officer.

#3390. The 35+ Best Gifts for Moms, According to My Mother’s Mini Me (Yours Truly)

If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Rolling Stone may receive an affiliate commission.

They say mother knows best, and when it comes to gift-giving, mine really does. My mom has always had a flair for whimsy. She’s the kind of woman who would lay an entire tarp across our backyard on the last day of school and stage a food fight, or build a Christmas countdown calendar from scratch, then fill every little compartment with surprises.

She’s also the reason I learned that the best gifts aren’t necessarily the ones people ask for, but the ones they didn’t even know they needed. Turns out, that lesson would come in handy when I made gift-giving my career.

My mom is truly the best human on the planet. Don’t worry, I’m sure yours is, too. Which is why I want to help you find a present she’ll love when the holidays roll around.

So, where do you start shopping? I’d steer clear of the obvious. Sure, a robe is nice. A scarf will keep her warm. Another water bottle? She probably has six. You can do better! This is the woman who taught you how to make the most out of life, after all. She deserves something as one-of-a-kind as your relationship. Maybe that’s a cuckoo clock you can build together or a custom garden gnome with her face on it. Whatever fills her cup, there’s something here that’ll make her smile.

I also kept budgets, interests, and personalities in mind, because no two moms — or gift-givers — are alike. Hanukkah, Christmas, and some of the biggest shopping holidays of the year are fast approaching (and didn’t your mom teach you that early is always better than on time?). So consider this your friendly nudge to get shopping. For Hanukkah, aim to have your gifts sorted by around Nov. 20, roughly two weeks before the holiday. For Christmas, I’d try to wrap things up by Dec. 12.

Shop my 35+ best gifts for your mom below, and give her something she’ll actually want to show off to her friends. You know, something other than another photo of you.

Cozy Earth pajamas have been one of the most popular products in all of our holiday gift guides, and for good reason. Between their near-unreasonable level of softness and my own personal devotion to them, they had to make this list too. They run true to size, but if you’re debating sizing up, I say go for it. The worst thing that can happen is she ends up even more comfortable.

Gorjana makes stunning birthstone bracelets that you can customize with stones representing her kids, grandkids, or whoever else has earned a spot. Or, you can leave everyone else off and just include yourself… A subtle way to remind her who her favorite child is.

If your mom spends as much time in the garden as she does with your dad — potentially more, no judgment — get her a custom garden gnome with her face on it. All you have to do is provide a photo, and Printerval handles the rest.

Have you hugged your mom recently? If not, I’m going to need you to get on that. But even the most devoted children can’t be there all the time, and sometimes she might need a little extra comfort when you’re not around. This Bearaby weighted blanket is a pretty good stand-in. Just don’t let it replace an actual phone call.

This might be one of the sweetest gifts you can buy your mom this holiday season because chances are she owned a version of this Lenox Spice Village when she was little, or her mom did. Either way, it’s the kind of nostalgic gift that can transport her back to simpler times while also giving her kitchen a very cute upgrade. My mother-in-law had the original, so I got her this modern version for Christmas this year (and Cara, if you see this, pretend you didn’t).

If you thought Tommy Bahama only made resort wear for vacations in the Bahamas, allow me to introduce you to the brand’s winter staples. This fleece jacket is insanely comfortable, and I own multiple Tommy Bahama sweaters that have convinced me the quality is the real deal. Take my word for it; I shop for a living.

My mom reads about three books a week, no exaggeration, so making sure she never loses her place is practically a public service. I got her this page-saving cottage lamp, which doubles as a cute little bedside accessory. It adds a bit of whimsy to her literary world and means she can stop folding the corners of her books. (Please tell her not to do that.)

And since she’s so obsessed with reading, I also got her this literature mug from Uncommon Goods, which happens to be one of my favorite places to find genuinely unique gifts. She just has to scan it with her phone (and if she doesn’t have an upgraded smartphone yet, maybe that’s your next gift) to hear from some of the world’s greatest literary minds whenever she wants.

Treat your mom to tea for two (with you, obviously) by buying her this stunning Spode china set. It’s currently on sale at Macy’s, and as someone who was recently gifted her own set of nice china, I can tell you that opening a box like this might just take her breath away. Which, really, is how you win Christmas. Not that it’s a competition…

For that beautiful china you just got her, help her preserve it with this stunning display cabinet from Ashley Furniture. It fits perfectly into just about any corner of her home and gives her a place to show off all of her favorite mementos. Maybe your eighth-grade art project won’t make the cut, but her mother’s wedding spoon might.

So, yes, this might be one of the more basic Christmas gifts on the list, but you seriously can’t go wrong with getting your mom a pair of house shoes. And if you’re going to do it, make them UGGs. They’re a chic way to give her slippers that feel a little more thoughtful than the random pair you panic-bought from a massive online retailer two days before Christmas.

This is a more practical gift for your mom, but it’s also one she probably didn’t know existed or that she needed. Memory Air works by releasing scented puffs while she sleeps and claims to do everything from helping her get more ZZZs at night to reinforcing memory, according to the brand. Plus, it’s “supported by scientific research,” so your mom doesn’t have to worry that this is another random thing you were served in a suspicious Instagram ad. I regret the minute I ever told my mom about those.

For the moms who love birdwatching, this high-tech feeder lets her see who’s making a pit stop through a connected app. It can even help identify the species, which is a whole lot easier than trying to describe a bird to an AI website and hoping for the right answer.

My mom has been making us pajama pants for Christmas for as long as I can remember, so I recently decided to upgrade her sewing machine and make her job a little easier. She hasn’t stopped telling me how much she loves this model. It’s great for easy projects, more challenging ones, and even the things she didn’t know were possible. Her mom used a Singer, my mom uses a Singer, and I use a Singer, too. Three generations in, I think we can call that a family endorsement.

My mom and I went to Austria together in September and walked into a cuckoo clock shop. We both knew immediately that we had to buy one. If your mom shares the same wandering spirit as the two of us, get her one she can build herself — or, even better, one you can help her put together. Consider it an excuse to spend a little more time together.

If your mom is the kind of woman who would happily spend the rest of her life in comfortable clothes, you’re doing her a disservice by not getting her this Aviator Nation sweatshirt and matching sweatpants. It delivers everything she loves about her favorite sweatshirt, just in a version she can actually leave the house in. The one with your childhood fingerprints all over it is cute, but maybe it’s time to move that one into the memory box.

Tinggly is one of my personal gifting hacks because it gives your mom more than another thing to unwrap under the tree; it gives her an experience. And, realistically, the thing she probably wants most is to spend time with you. A weekend getaway is a pretty great way to make that happen. This package lets her choose from multiple destinations, so you can give her the R&R she deserves without pretending you know exactly where she wants to go. Use code ROLLING to get 40% off your order.

If I had to guess, your mom has been carrying the same tired shoulder bag for approximately a decade. Give her a much-deserved upgrade with this Rebecca Minkoff and Grace Ann Nader hobo bag. Bonus points if she’s a Real Housewives fan, since Rebecca Minkoff is a RHONY alum.

For the mom who prefers her nightly reading to be more of a listening experience, give her an Audible subscription. The platform gives her access to audiobooks from some of the most popular authors, all for just $8.99 a month. Better yet, her first three months cost less than $1. My mom was hesitant about audiobooks at first, but now says listening is one of her favorite pastimes, whether she’s driving in the car or getting ready in the morning.

If your mom is anything like mine, she prides herself on being the hostess with the mostest (I think she gives Martha Stewart a run for her money). Make her kitchen duties a little easier this holiday season with a premade charcuterie board from Boarderie. You can choose your preferred size, with plenty of combinations featuring everything from meats and cheeses to savory spreads.

There’s a TikTok trend going around where daughters dress their mothers up as cooler, more fashionable versions of themselves. And while I’m not saying your mom needs a complete wardrobe overhaul (unless she’s asking), a little style upgrade never hurt anyone. These Maui Jim sunglasses are a great place to start.

My mom is always asking me about my skincare routine, and instead of giving her my full Get Ready With Me speech every time she brings it up, I finally just sent her the link to this Water Whip moisturizer. It’s a no-frills but extremely functional way to keep your skin looking close to perfect, and now she uses it every morning and, apparently, has made it her personal mission to tell all of her friends about it too.

Even dog moms are mothers, so if you’re shopping for the woman in your life who treats her pet like her actual baby (as she should), this Lola dog bed (yes, that Lola) will help her spoil her little furry bundle of joy accordingly. Since getting one for my dog, he hasn’t left it for more than 20 minutes at a time. Plus, I appreciate how good it actually looks in my home, which is something I can’t say about every dog bed.

Brilliant Earth has some of our favorite gift ideas for Mom, but this special necklace is as tasteful as it gets. It’s dainty, affordable, and best of all, it comes from you. Pearls supposedly symbolize motherhood and everlasting love, so what better way to put that sentiment into something tangible than with this pendant?

I recently got my mom this bedding bundle, and one morning I woke up to a text that read: “OMG, OMG, OMG, this is the best set of sheets ever!!!! I didn’t want to get out of bed!! Do I have to go to work?? LOL.” True story. So, if you want to wake up to a similarly enthusiastic review from your own mother, this is a pretty safe bet.

Myles Price makes sweatshirts for every kind of mom, especially the hot mamas who want to be comfortable but still look like they have their lives together. She’ll be the envy of every other parent at school pickup, and almost definitely the most comfortable one there.

I feel a little guilty about this one. I’ve known about Lola Blankets for a while now, own multiple, and am about as obsessed with them as the rest of the internet. Then my mom called me the other day to say she saw one on TV and was dying to get one…. Something I probably should have gotten her months ago. Well, I immediately ordered it, and now it’s on its way. Learn from my mistakes and do the same for your mother before it’s too late and they sell out of her Christmas list.

My mom has been wearing this scent for decades, and she always told me that you can never go wrong with Chanel. You know what? She was right (as she is about a lot of things). This was also reportedly one of Marilyn Monroe’s favorite scents, and while some gentlemen might prefer blondes, your mom will probably prefer this perfume.

Getting your mom another picture of yourself is so last year. What she really wants under the tree is a portrait of her dog as a member of the royal court. I was gifted one of these a few years ago and have been slowly getting them for all of my family members ever since. My mom hangs hers in what she calls her parlor, also known as the billiards room. Whatever you call the room, this deserves a spot in it.

For the moms who are fans of The Mary Tyler Moore Show, you can now get her some of the most iconic looks she saw on screen, thanks to this collaboration with Frances Valentine. How’s that for actually paying attention to her hobbies and getting her something she probably wouldn’t think to buy herself?

If you have a wife who recently became a mom, get her these Hot Mom socks so she can remember exactly who the hell she is, even in the thick of postpartum life. Did I send this link to my brother so he could get them for his wife, who just had a baby? Yes. Do I know she’ll appreciate the reminder? More than you think. Take it from a woman.

My mom and I ran our first-ever 5K in Brooks sneakers, and while we might not be adding marathons to our regularly scheduled mother-daughter activities anytime soon, one thing we’ll continue doing together is wearing Brooks. They’re the only sneakers my mom will buy, and considering she works retail and spends eight hours a day on her feet, I trust her judgment.

Your mom is already the head of your family’s team, but if she has another team she roots for — or a specific player she loves, like Josh Allen (all moms love him, it’s a fact) — help her show her support with a cute sweatshirt from ’47 and Stoney Clover Lane. They run slightly bigger than your average crewneck, so size down if she prefers a more fitted look.

Moms everywhere are obsessed with mahjong. That might be a generalization, but I know mine is, as are all of my aunts and cousins who are moms. Help her get in on the game-night action with a set of her very own. She’ll be the most popular person at the next family gathering.

I always say you should buy your mom a pair of recovery slides from Nike because they help her take a load off, quite literally. But then I found this upgraded version from Nike x Hyperice that actually heats up and massages her feet. Yeah, that’s an automatic win.

If your mom is obsessed with all things Disney, pay tribute to one of her favorite pastimes with this Lilly Pulitzer and Disney dress. It’s a little less Mickey Mouse and a little more subtly infused magic, thanks to a classic Lilly Pulitzer silhouette she can wear outside the parks, too.

My mom is always cold. She probably doesn’t realize that she spent 20 years of her life sitting through my brothers’ ice hockey games, but I’m pretty sure that’s where it started. So I got her this Carhartt jacket, which manages to keep her at just the right temperature even during a brutal New Hampshire winter. If anyone knows how to dress for a chilly day, it’s a hockey mom.

At some point in time, your mom will become obsessed with her family tree (if it hasn’t happened already). The day my mom told me we were distantly related to a European king was the greatest day of her life, which only mildly concerned me. Help her dig into her past with an Ancestry DNA kit. You never know who your mom might discover she’s related to, or which royal family she might try to claim as her own.

For the moms whose love language is a Sunday supper (which was definitely my nanny’s), get her these world-class pans from Eater and Heritage Steel. She can whip up anything, from meatballs to her own top-secret gravy recipe, and you’ll benefit from the results. Or, better yet, make her a meal with them. She deserves it, after all.

This gift is for both the moms who love to garden and those who want to but might not exactly have a green thumb. I’ll tell you this: When I first bought one for myself, I was skeptical. But it supplied my husband and me with six months of the freshest vegetables I’ve ever tasted, after which I immediately ordered more seedling pods. When my parents found out about it, they ordered one, too, and my mom says she’d never go back to traditional gardening. That’s a pretty strong endorsement.

#3389. Why Apple shouldn’t worry about iPhone Duo returns

A poll of 9to5Mac readers who were lucky enough to take delivery of their iPhone Duo in the first few days shows that 30% of them have returned it for a refund.

While that could be considered bad news for the future of the device, I don’t personally consider it either surprising or worrying …

Following a report by The Verge on iPhone Duo buyers who opted to return the device for a refund within Apple’s 14-day “no questions asked” period, we thought it would be interesting to get a sense of how many people may have done this.

9to5Mac readers were always likely to have had their fingers hovering over the pre-order button for the best shot at taking early delivery, with the first of these having hit the end of the 14-day window. We ask those of you who fall into this category to tell us whether you kept or returned the device.

With close to 6,000 total votes, the results showed that close to a third of you returned your Duo.

For any other device, that would be a disastrous return rate. For the Duo, however, I don’t think it’s terribly surprising.

I voted to say I returned it just so I could see the results. I’ve never ordered nor returned an iPhone Duo.

Not providing a way to see the results without voting will have massively skewed the results. Even if the poll were better, this is a wild claim to draw from one specific, poorly assembled assembled poll.

As we noted yesterday, Apple described the iPhone Duo as “the most transformational change to iPhone since the original.” The size of that change shows up in a whole range of ways, from the weight of the device through the changed aspect ratio of the front display to a completely new way of using an iPhone.

Throw in the extremely high price tag, and I’ve always suspected that a significant number of iPhone Duo buyers would be viewing it as an experiment rather than a committed purchase. Our own Ryan Christoffel is an example of that “try it and see” attitude. One week in, he’s reached an interim conclusion that it’s probably not for him.

For those who’ve decided to return it, a number of readers shared their reasons.

“Returned it – I can’t go back to Touch ID.”

“I want to like it, but I just can’t get there. It’s awkward, and the outside screen is way too small.”

“Returned it. Not for me. I do not want to open the phone every time I want a larger screen and Apple made the outer display much less usable than it should be with that silly permanent dock. I also use my phones left-handed.”

“During a vacation in Morocco, we spent a night camping in the Sahara Desert. I was extremely careful with the phone and tried to avoid using it in the sand altogether. However, on the second day, when I opened it inside the tent, I heard a crunching sound coming from the hinge. Sand had somehow gotten inside. I tried everything I could to clean it, but nothing worked. The inner display was still functioning perfectly, but the phone would no longer open all the way. Even worse, when I tried to close it, I had to force it shut.”

For me personally, it couldn’t be my only phone, given the priority I place on the device as a camera, but I am still lusting after it. Given the continued extended delivery times – with random checks showing shipping in late January – I don’t think Apple has much to worry about here.

#3388. Top Wall Street analysts prefer these dividend stocks for boosting portfolio returns

Dividend stocks remain a popular choice for investors seeking steady income and higher portfolio returns. However, with thousands of dividend-paying companies to choose from, identifying the right stocks can be challenging.

In this regard, recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can provide useful insights and help identify dividend stocks backed by solid fundamentals and with attractive upside potential.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Independent oil and natural gas company Permian Resources (PR) is this week's first dividend stock. The company recently paid a quarterly base cash dividend of 16 cents per share. At an annualized dividend of 64 cents per share, PR offers a dividend yield of 3.5%.

Recently, Evercore analyst Chris Baker initiated coverage of Permian Resources stock with a price target of $25. The analyst believes that the company is well positioned to benefit from improving U.S. shale demand after the Iran conflict, thanks to its low-breakeven inventory that can boost free cash flow growth. Baker also noted PR's disciplined consolidation in the Permian Basin.

Furthermore, the 5-star analyst highlighted the company's focus on a single basin and management's efficient capital allocations across expansion efforts, strategic acquisitions, and share buybacks. Baker noted that management focuses investments on the higher-return Northern Delaware Basin, helping boost profitability.

"The key piece of our work here, and the reason we think PR deserves a higher multiple relative to more finite or less flexible shale stories, is that PR runs an acquire and exploit model," said Baker.

He explained that Permian Resources deserves a premium valuation as it continually acquires and develops new high-quality assets instead of relying on a limited inventory, a strategy that is the market is underappreciating.

Baker ranks No. 862 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 48.3%. See Permian Resources Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Valero Energy (VLO) is a manufacturer and marketer of petroleum-based and low-carbon liquid transportation fuels and petrochemical products. At a quarterly dividend of $1.20 per share, or annualized dividend of $4.80 per share, VLO stock offers a yield of about 2%.

Heading into Valero's second-quarter earnings on July 30, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on VLO stock and increased the price target to $286 from $283 to reflect updated estimates.

Specifically, the 5-star analyst raised his 2026 and 2027 earnings per share estimates to $31.42 and $23.07 from $29.42 and $21.06, respectively, while leaving the 2028 EPS estimate unchanged at $20.37. Mehta made these revisions based on several factors, including updated commodity price assumptions and changes to refining capture rates.

Despite a strong year-to-date rally in VLO stock, Mehta still finds it compelling due to his more positive refining outlook. Moreover, the analyst sees the possibility of solid estimate revisions, which could drive the stock higher. He believes that Valero is well-positioned to benefit from improving refining market conditions due to its strong position in the Gulf Coast, solid balance sheet strength, and low-cost operations.

"Additionally, we believe the company's premium asset portfolio and crude slate optionality should support capture rates and stronger cash flow generation in the near-term, ultimately supporting shareholder returns," said Mehta.

Mehta ranks No. 742 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 59% of the time, delivering an average return of 10.2%. See Valero Energy Statistics on TipRanks.

Moving on to Ovintiv (OVV), a North American oil and natural gas producer. It has solid positions in North America's premier oil basins – the Permian and the Montney. OVV offers a quarterly dividend of 30 cents per share, or an annualized dividend of $1.20 per share, implying a 2.3% yield.

Following meetings with management, RBC Capital analyst Gregory Pardy reaffirmed a buy rating on Ovintiv stock with a price target of $70, highlighting that the stock is on RBC's Global Energy Best Ideas List.

"In our eyes, the depth of Ovintiv's Montney position, streamlined portfolio, strong balance sheet and enhanced shareholder returns afford investors with an attractive valuation re-rating opportunity over time," said Pardy.

The 5-star analyst stated that his meetings with management bolstered his confidence in the company's outlook and potential to achieve a higher valuation. Pardy noted Ovintiv's transformation, with the company streamlining its portfolio from six basins (including the Uinta, Bakken and Anadarko) to two – the Montney and Permian – while enhancing the depth of its inventory.

Pardy also emphasized OVV's improved shareholder returns and solid balance sheet following the recent sale of its assets in the Anadarko Basin for $3 billion.

Pardy ranks No. 169 among more than 12,300 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 22.3%. See Ovintiv Options Trading Activity on TipRanks.

#3387. Shakira Goes Global, Drake Gets Love, and More Latin Music Takeaways from the 2027 Grammy Nominations

The Recording Academy doesn’t always get it right when it comes to Latin music, but lately they’ve been trying. Last year, voters from the Latin Recording Academy were able to cast ballots in the standard edition, making for a more diverse voting pool. It’s a move that’s already paid off. Earlier this year, at the 2026 awards, Bad Bunny made history with the first Album of the Year win for a full Spanish-language album. Now, with the 2027 Grammy nominations, one of the biggest genres in the U.S. is still front and center — even if some of the nods are perplexing. Let’s take a look at all of the Latin music highlights from this year’s nominations.

Rosalía just made history at the Latin Grammys when she became the first woman to win Album of the Year three times. Now, the Spanish singer is the second-most-decorated nominee for the 2027 Grammys, and she could follow Bad Bunny’s lead with another historic AOTY win. If Rosalía’s Lux snags the highest honor of the night, she would become the first woman to win in the category with a Spanish-language project.

There were a handful of Latin music first-time nominees across categories. Ryan Castro secured two nods in the Best Música Urbana Album, one for his solo LP Hopi Sendé and another for his collaborative album with J Balvin, Omerta. Meanwhile, Argentine musician Milo J earned recognition in the Best Latin Song and Best Latin Rock or Alternative Album categories for his Latin Grammy-winning project La vida era Más Corta. Venezuelan American singer Elena Rose also received her first-ever Grammy nod, in the Best Latin Pop Album category. About that…

… Rose’s nomination leads us to the unfortunate catch-all that the Best Latin Pop Album category became this year. As we said, the Academy doesn’t always get it right when it comes to Latin music. Nowhere is that more blatant than this category, which is jam-packed with an array of popular Latin artists who make distinct music from each other. Karol G’s alternative album No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto makes some sense here, as does Mon Laferte’s Femme Fatale — but Carín León’s Muda runs the gamut of genres from norteño to salsa and soul. It makes no sense here, and Rawayana’s and Elena Rose’s genre-bending albums don’t really, either. Rather than find a way to honor these impressive works and the widely varied Latin genres they’re pushing forward, the Academy seems to be stuffing them under one confusing umbrella. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

Drake is up for Best Latin Song. Yes, you read that right: The rap superstar has received a nod for his Spanish-language feature on Karol G’s “Ahí.” It’s surprising in many ways, but especially considering Drake’s longstanding differences with the Academy; the last time he won a Grammy for one of his own songs, in 2019, he gave a speech about how little the awards mean to him, and he’s chosen not to submit his own work since then. The fact that the Academy nominated “Ahí” rather than Karol’s Bruno Mars collaboration “Still” is also a bit of a head-scratcher. But now Champagne Papi will go up against acts like Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso, Rosalía, Milo J, and Jorge Drexler. Trending Stories Raye, Rosalía, and Ella Langley Lead 2027 Grammy Nominees Jennifer Lopez Teases New Music on ‘Fallon’: ‘This Does Feel Like a Happy Era’ Watch Buffalo Springfield Come Together for the First Time in Many Years Robert Pattinson Is the Next James Bond

One of Latin music’s most sought-after collaborators is being recognized by the Academy once more. Edgar Barrera nabbed a third consecutive nod for Songwriter of the Year, Non-Classical. He’s up against a field that includes Amy Allen and Theron Thomas, both of whom previously beat him. But after working on some of the year’s biggest Latin music projects and writing for Gracie Abrams, could this finally be the year the Recording Academy honors Barrera’s songwriting power?

There’s no denying Latin music’s worldwide takeover — just look at what Shakira and Anitta are doing. Both stars submitted their music beyond the Latin music categories, and they were recognized for continuing to expand their reach. Anitta’s latest album, Equilibrivm, received a nod for Best Global Music Album, while Shakira’s World Cup hit “Dai Dai” was nominated for Best Global Music Performance.

#3386. Foxconn revenue climbs 46%; Bloomberg forecasts 16M iPhone Duo sales

Key Apple manufacturing partner Foxconn has announced a year-on-year revenue increase of 46%, thanks to a mix of consumer electronics and server demand.

Separately, Bloomberg Intelligence has forecast sales of 16 million iPhone Duo units in the first 12 months …

Foxconn is by far the largest contract manufacturer for iPhones, and at one point the majority of its revenue came from Apple. That hasn’t been true for some time, however, largely because of the company’s rapid expansion into servers for AI data centers and cloud storage.

All the same, some 29% of its revenue still comes from its consumer electronics division, of which Apple is by far the largest customer. It’s likely that at least some of its growth comes from the assembly of Apple products.

That’s backed by Bloomberg Intelligence prediction that sales of the iPhone Duo may hit 16 million units by September of next year. That would be well above earlier expectations, with Apple reportedly targeting 9.7M units in the first year before strong demand saw the company raise the goal to 14M.

Bloomberg says that with overall global smartphone demand decreasing due to a difficult economic environment, premium models like the Duo will become increasingly important to Apple’s revenue and profit.

The new app is currently in testing and will roll out fully from early next year.

#3384. Trump Lashes Out at ‘Loser’ Reporter for Questioning D.C. Renovation Obsession

A defensive Donald Trump lashed out at a reporter who asked him to justify why he was spending so much time renovating Washington, D.C., as opposed to more pressing issues like the aging air traffic control system, which glitched on Friday, abruptly halting air travel across the country for the longest period since the terrorist attacks on September 11, 2001.

“What do you say to critics who say you were too focused on D.C. construction projects while our airline systems were crumbling?” Trump was asked outside the White House on Monday.

“If you take a look at the White House, it’s flawless,” Trump replied.

But the question clearly touched a nerve because the president continued: “Listen to me, I know you don’t see dirt. But if you take a look at the White House — you’d never notice broken windows obviously from where you come.” Trump was speaking to NBC White House Correspondent Yamiche Alcindor, who is of Haitian descent.

Trump went on to declare, “The helipad has gotten great reviews,” while ignoring Alcindor’s follow-up questions about the weekend disruptions at airports across the U.S.

“Oh, you’re so pathetic,” Trump said as Alcindor pressed him about whether he and the Republican Party should have taken responsibility for not securing adequate funding to pay for upgrades to the air traffic control system. “I have a responsibility to make sure the symbol of our country is in decent shape — and it takes me 10 minutes a day. Very little time.”

“This doesn’t cost money. This is peanuts. This is called talent. Talent. You don’t have talent,” Trump said, continuing to insult the reporter. “The White House was in terrible condition, now it’s in beautiful condition. Cost me very little money to do it very little time to do and losers like you come out and say ‘Why are you focused on the White House?’”

Trump’s quest to reshape D.C. in his ideal image has resulted in an endless string of headlines and legal cases. Every year, countless artists have their hopes and dreams dashed when the Recording Academy reveals its nominees for the Grammy Awards. For the most part, the unfortunately snubbed choose to lick their wounds in private. Maybe they toss out an oblique or pithy quip on social media. Or maybe they make a video like Muna’s Katie Gavin, who copped to feeling disappointed, discussed the challenges of trying to shoehorn the band’s music into the Grammys’ sometimes overly-rigid genre categories, and still celebrated the artists who did get nominated.

But few show the chutzpah of DJ-producer John Summit, who took to X to proclaim, “Never submitting to the Grammys again unless shit changes, it’s all a fucking joke.”

never submitting to the grammys again unless shit changes, it’s all a fucking joke. i’m not just talking about myself either there’s zero respect for real electronic dance music & dj’s. the whole dance category is just music industry fueled pop stars

It is true that that the dance and EDM categories didn’t really feature any top-line DJs/producers besides Fred Again and Skrillex. #3381. 10 Hacks Every Hulu User Should Know

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

If you don't like the content Hulu is suggesting for you, you have several options to curate your recommendations. "Disliking" a show or movie removes it from your Home view and You May Also Like entirely, so the only way you'll see that content is if you search for it. You can dislike on the Details page if you're watching on your TV or use the thumbs down on mobile or web. (The "Like" button will obviously influence your algorithm in the opposite way). If your "Continue Watching" queue is cluttered with shows you started but didn't like enough to finish, you can remove them from your watch history as well as the My Stuff list. This, too, will allow content to remain searchable but not suggested in other areas of the app.

If PIN protection is enabled, users must enter a four-digit PIN when switching between profiles on a single account. This is intended as a parental control feature, since it's available on non-Kids profiles and can keep children from accessing more mature content on an adult's profile. However, you can also enable this feature to keep other users from seeing your viewing history and preferences or influencing your algorithm by watching their content under your profile (accidentally or on purpose). To set up a PIN, log into your account on Hulu's website, select your profile, and go to Manage Profiles > Parental Controls. You'll have to choose a PIN and enter your password to confirm the changes.

Another approach to protecting your profile and algorithm is to set up separate profiles for specific use cases, such as when you have guests or if you host watch parties for certain shows. This keeps content from influencing your recommendations and prevents other viewers from seeing what's in your watch history or saved content (especially if there are things you want to keep private).

If you find that subtitles and captions are too bold—or not visible enough—you can change the font, color, size, and style from the default so they enhance your viewing experience rather than detracting from it. Hulu allows you to adjust the color and opacity of the font, background, and window so you get the right contrast, and you can also select the specific font and font scaling. On your streaming device, go to Settings > Subtitles & Captions, then hit the back button on your remote to save your preferences. You can update these settings on mobile and desktop as well.

If you have a long list of shows and films to watch but can't decide what to start next, look for the "Expiring Soon" badge to see which titles are leaving the service in the next two weeks. Badges display the number of days remaining, so you can determine what to prioritize and whether it's worth diving in based on how much time you have to finish before the expiration date. Go to "My Stuff" to monitor saved titles that are expiring soon.

If you've been watching Hulu under an account shared with family or friends and need to switch to your own subscription, you can transfer your profile to keep your watch history and settings intact instead of starting from scratch. You can initiate a profile transfer on a TV-connected device. Note that account holders have to approve transfer requests within seven days, and once expired, transfer requests cannot be resubmitted—so be sure to let the primary user know that you've made the request.

If you've shared your Hulu login information with friends or activated your account on devices you don't own, you may want to regularly audit where your account is being used and remove any that don't need access. This includes TVs in Airbnbs and hotels. If you stay logged in, unauthorized users may have access to your Hulu account and personal data. You can see activated devices (and their activation date) under Your Account > Watch Hulu on Your Devices > Manage Devices. Click Remove next to old or unrecognized devices.

Hulu has an offline mode that allows you to download shows and movies to watch when you don't have a network connection. This is useful for traveling or when you know your wifi or cell service will be limited. Downloads are only available on supported iOS and Android devices, which means you may have to consider how much space your content takes up. You can select High for video quality if you want maximum resolution, but you may want to choose Standard if you are short on storage. This option is available under Downloads > Settings > Video Quality on iOS and Account > Settings > Downloads > Video Quality on Android. Note that once you click play on downloaded content, you have 48 hours to watch it before it expires—so don't start it unless you are ready.

If you have a Hulu + Live TV subscription, you must designate a "Home" network, which determines the local channels included in your plan. You can update your location up to four times within a 12-month period, but this limitation is meant to prevent viewers outside a household from sharing a subscription. Hulu does allow you to stream live TV on mobile when you're away from your home network (within the U.S.) as long as you access your account on that network every 30 days. If you travel often, check in with your mobile device frequently to avoid being locked out when you're away. Note that you can still watch streaming content with no restrictions.

#3380. Jensen Huang resigns as CEO of Nvidia

Jensen Huang has resigned as the CEO of Nvidia following recent reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman suspected of spying for China. Here are the details.

In late October, The New York Times reported on Jensen Huang’s “close relationship” with Alice Huang, a former managing director at Singapore-based Megaspeed, whom US intelligence officials reportedly identified as a Chinese intelligence asset suspected of passing information to Beijing.

According to subsequent reports, Chinese intelligence allegedly recruited her to gather information about Jensen Huang and influence his position on selling advanced AI chips to Chinese companies. China disputes the espionage allegations, dismissing them as groundless speculation intended to smear the country.

That said, while Nvidia previously denied any impropriety in their relationship, Huang admitted last weekend to having an extramarital affair in a message to employees, saying, “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did.” He did not mention Alice Huang directly.

In the following days, concerns grew over the potential national security implications of the relationship, in addition to Nvidia seeing its stock plummet.

And while Huang remained CEO as Nvidia’s board commissioned an independent investigation into the allegations, The New York Times reported on Wednesday that he had a second extramarital affair, this time with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him.

In the hours that followed, The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board was preparing to meet to decide Huang’s future. Soon after, Semafor reported that some board members favored Nvidia CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO, while other reports suggested that Huang’s daughter, Madison Huang, could eventually succeed him. Madison Huang works at Nvidia as senior director of product marketing.

Semafor also named Apple’s chief hardware officer, Johny Srouji, as a potential successor, while Bloomberg reported that Nvidia had hired an outside firm to identify candidates.

Now, Nvidia has officially announced that Huang “has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately.”

The company confirmed that Kress has been appointed interim CEO, while retaining her current responsibilities, until a permanent successor is named. The company is considering both internal and external candidates.

Nvidia also announced that Harvey C. Jones, a longtime technology executive and venture investor, has been appointed the company’s first-ever board chair.

In a statement, Jones said the board has “full confidence in Colette and the leadership team,” adding that Nvidia expects its operations, customer commitments, and product roadmap to continue without interruption.

The shareholder lawsuits over the broad-spectrum mismanagement are going to be incredible.

No succession plan. Lying to investors to cover up the CEO’s unethical and foolish behavior. Having a super-weak board of directors absent anyone with high-level relevant experience.

Nvidia did not directly address the allegations surrounding Huang in its announcement, instead thanking him for his contributions to the company over the past 33 years.

Following the Times’ Wednesday report, Nvidia shares plunged in after-hours trading, erasing the day’s 2.9% gain after two consecutive sessions of losses.

The stock continued to fall following today’s announcement, dropping more than 10% at the time of writing from Wednesday’s closing price of $173.73, bringing its total decline to approximately 35% from its October 6 record close.

How Nvidia’s stock will behave when the market opens today and in the days that follow is anyone’s guess, especially with the company scheduled to report its quarterly earnings next Tuesday, November 17.
